transcript.text: my washin mashine wont turn on at all no lights nothin

That's frustrating! When there are no lights at all, it's usually a power problem rather than the machine itself, so start with the easy stuff:

1. Check the plug
• Make sure it's pushed all the way into the wall (machines vibrate and can work it loose).
• Look at the cord and plug for any damage, burn marks, or melting. If you see any, stop and don't use it.

2. Test the outlet
• Plug something else in (a lamp, phone charger, hair dryer) to see if the outlet works.
• If the machine is plugged into a power strip or extension cord, plug it directly into the wall instead.

3. Check the circuit breaker / fuse box
• Look for a tripped breaker (one that's flipped to "off" or sitting in the middle). Flip it fully off, then back on.
• If it trips again right away, there may be a fault. Leave it off and call an electrician or repair person.

4. Check for a GFCI outlet
• In laundry rooms, outlets often have "Test" and "Reset" buttons. Press Reset firmly. Sometimes the GFCI is on a different outlet nearby (bathroom, garage, or kitchen) that controls this one too.

5. Reset the machine
• Unplug it for 5 to 10 minutes, then plug it back in. This can clear a glitch in the electronics.

6. Check the door/lid and child lock
• Some machines look "dead" if the door isn't fully latched or child lock is on (often by holding a button combo for 3 seconds; check your manual).

If none of that works, the problem is likely inside the machine, such as:
• A blown internal fuse
• A faulty power switch or door lock
• A failed control board

Those usually need a repair technician, especially if it's still under warranty.

If you tell me the brand and model (usually on a sticker inside the door or on the back), I can give you more specific tips. And did anything happen right before it stopped, like a power outage, storm, or strange noise?
its built in behind a cupboard door so i cant get to the plug or see any label. the kettle works tho and the fridge. its not tripped anything at the fuse box, all switches up

Since the kettle and fridge work and nothing's tripped, the power to the house is fine. The problem is likely between the wall and the machine. With built-in machines there's often a separate switch you can't easily see, so check these:

1. Look for a switch above the worktop
Built-in appliances usually have their own switch since the plug is hidden. Look on the wall above the counter near the machine, or in a row of switches (sometimes labelled "washer," "dishwasher," etc.).
• Make sure it's switched on (someone may have knocked it).
• Many of these switches have a small fuse slot on the front. If the fuse has blown, the machine gets no power even though everything else works.

2. Replace that fuse (if there is one)
• Switch it off first.
• Use a flat screwdriver to pop out the little fuse holder.
• Swap in a new 13 amp fuse (cheap at supermarkets/DIY shops, or borrow one from a plug that's not in use, as long as it says 13A).
• Switch back on and try the machine.

If the new fuse blows again straight away, stop there. That points to a fault in the machine, so it's time for a repair person.

3. Check the door
Open and firmly close the machine door. If it isn't latched properly, some machines won't light up at all.

Finding the model label
Open the washing machine door itself. The sticker is usually on the rim around the door opening or on the inside edge of the door. That'll give the brand and model if you need a repair or want more specific help.

If there's no switch anywhere and the door is fine, the next step would be sliding the machine out to check the plug, which is awkward, so a repair person might be worth it at that point. Did you find a switch above the counter?

ok i found a row of switches above the worktop and the one saying washer was off, my flatmate must of switched it off when she was cleaning. i turned it back on and the machine lights up now and works!

Great news, glad it was something that simple! Those switches get knocked off all the time, especially when someone's wiping down the worktop.

If it keeps happening, a little sticky note or label saying "leave on" next to the switch can save you the same head-scratching next time.

Happy washing!
